healthcareSystem: Very limited public healthcare. Hospitals are underfunded and poorly equipped. A few private clinics in Nouakchott offer marginally better care. Outside the capital, medical facilities are extremely basic or nonexistent.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is very limited. Chronic shortage of doctors, equipment, and medications. Arabic and French are the medical languages. English-speaking doctors are very rare. Bring a comprehensive medical kit and all needed medications.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Nouakchott open 8am-6pm, some with a midday break. Very limited pharmacy access outside the capital.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Nouakchott stock basic medications but supply is inconsistent. Counterfeit drugs are a concern. French and Arabic spoken at pharmacies. Bring all essential medications from home.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is minimal. Medication quality and authenticity are concerns. French or Arabic prescriptions expected. Bring all medications from home.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter in French or Arabic. Keep in original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Bring documentation from prescribing physician. Islamic law influences drug regulations.

restrictedMeds.name: Alcohol-based medications
restrictedMeds.note: Mauritania is an Islamic republic. Alcohol is prohibited. Alcohol-based medicines may be scrutinized at customs.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications, ideally in French or Arabic. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring generous extra supplies. A comprehensive personal medical kit is essential.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation is absolutely essential. Local healthcare is inadequate for serious conditions. Evacuation to Dakar, Casablanca, or Paris costs $40,000-120,000.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country; recommended for travel to southern regions. Malaria risk exists in the south — antimalarial prophylaxis recommended. Meningitis risk in dry season.

waterNotes: Tap water is not safe to drink anywhere in Mauritania. Always use bottled or purified water. In desert regions, bring ample water supplies. Use bottled water for brushing teeth.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only thoroughly cooked food served hot. Avoid raw salads and unpeeled fruits. Traditional dishes like thieboudienne (fish and rice) are generally safe when freshly prepared at restaurants. Avoid street food. Camel milk and meat should be well cooked.
medicalTourismNote: Mauritania is not a medical tourism destination. Patients needing specialist care travel to Dakar (Senegal), Casablanca (Morocco), or Paris.
metaDescription: Health guide for Mauritania: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, bottled water only, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Centre Hospitalier National (CHN)
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital in Mauritania. French and Arabic speaking. Basic equipment. Can be overcrowded.

hospitals.name: Clinique Chiva
hospitals.notes: Private clinic used by expatriates. Better equipment than public facilities. French and Arabic speaking.

hospitals.name: Polyclinique Teyarett
hospitals.notes: Private medical center. General consultations and basic emergency care. French-speaking.

hospitals.name: Hôpital Cheikh Zayed
hospitals.notes: Relatively newer hospital. Better infrastructure than CHN. French and Arabic speaking.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. A few dental clinics in Nouakchott only.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care quality is poor. Equipment may not meet international standards. French/Arabic speaking only.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: CHN has basic dental services. Private clinics in Nouakchott may offer faster service. Serious dental issues require evacuation.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Virtually none. French/Arabic-speaking counselors very limited.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are almost nonexistent. Bring all psychiatric medications from home with ample supply.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is virtually nonexistent. Roads are sandy or unpaved. Buildings lack ramps and wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Sand-covered roads make wheelchair use extremely difficult. 4x4 vehicles essential outside Nouakchott.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility impairments will face extreme challenges. Desert tourism (Chinguetti, Ouadane) involves rough terrain. Personal assistant and adapted vehicle essential. Plan all logistics far in advance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited testing available at hospitals in Nouakchott.
covidStatus.notes: Malaria, heat-related illness, dehydration, and waterborne diseases are far greater health concerns. Desert travel poses unique risks (heat stroke, sandstorms).

insuranceClaimProcess: Hospitals require upfront cash payment (Mauritanian Ouguiya). Facilities may not provide standardized receipts. Keep all documentation. Claims may require translation from French or Arabic.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Local currency is Mauritanian Ouguiya (MRU). Costs are low but quality is correspondingly limited.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is absolutely essential. Local healthcare cannot handle serious emergencies. Dakar is the nearest city with adequate hospitals. Desert evacuations may involve military or charter aircraft.

drugNameMap.note: French brands dominate. Doliprane is the most recognized. Arabic-labeled versions also available.
